novel_features.name: Multi-currency quote
novel_features.description: See any ticker's last price in its native currency, USD, and EUR in a single command.
novel_features.rationale: Community wrappers return a raw price in the instrument's own currency; only this CLI cross-fetches TradingView's forex rates and presents the price in USD and EUR together.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this when an agent needs a symbol's value normalized to USD or EUR without wiring up a separate FX API.

novel_features.name: TradingView-rate conversion
novel_features.description: Convert an amount between currencies using TradingView's own live forex rates.
novel_features.rationale: No TradingView wrapper exposes fiat conversion; this reuses TradingView forex symbols (FX_IDC:EURUSD, etc.) as the rate source so quotes and conversions share one data origin.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this to turn any USD figure into EUR (or between other majors) from the same source that priced the instrument.

novel_features.name: Local watchlist
novel_features.description: Track a list of symbols locally and snapshot their USD/EUR quotes to SQLite for offline querying.
novel_features.rationale: Local state that compounds: no TradingView wrapper persists a personal watchlist with multi-currency snapshots you can query offline.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this to keep a personal set of symbols and their USD/EUR prices without re-resolving them each call.

novel_features.name: Snapshot drift
novel_features.description: Show how each watched symbol moved in USD between its two most recent snapshots.
novel_features.rationale: Requires a local time series of snapshots that no single TradingView API call provides.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this to see what moved since your last sync without diffing raw API responses yourself.

narrative.headline: Resolve any ticker and see its price in USD and EUR in one command — stocks, crypto, and forex, no API key.
narrative.value_prop: TradingView CLI turns a symbol into an answer: search resolves a query to a fully-qualified EXCHANGE:TICKER, quote returns the last price in its native currency plus USD and EUR, and convert does fiat conversion using TradingView's own forex rates. Terminal-first, agent-native --json, no data-API subscription required for the public endpoints. A local watchlist tracks symbols and snapshots their USD/EUR prices to SQLite for offline querying and drift.

quickstart.comment: confirm the TradingView endpoints are reachable
resolve a query to a fully-qualified ticker like NASDAQ:AAPL (shows candidates)
last price in native currency, USD, and EUR
convert an amount using TradingView forex rates

troubleshoots.symptom: quote returns nothing for a bare ticker
troubleshoots.fix: run 'tradingview-pp-cli search <ticker>' first and use the fully-qualified EXCHANGE:TICKER

troubleshoots.symptom: crypto price shows currency USDT not USD
troubleshoots.fix: use a USD pair (e.g. COINBASE:ETHUSD) or read the price_usd field, which treats USDT as USD-pegged

narrative.when_to_use: Use this CLI when you need a fast, scriptable answer to 'what is <symbol> worth' in USD or EUR, for stocks, crypto, or forex, without a paid market-data API key. It is ideal for agents that must normalize a quote to a common currency.
anti_triggers: Do not use this CLI for placing trades or accessing a brokerage account — it is read-only market data.
Do not use it for historical OHLC backtesting datasets — it returns current quotes, not time series.
Do not use it for authenticated TradingView features like private watchlists or alerts — it targets public endpoints only.
